papers.title: Profinite rigidity of K\"ahler groups: Riemann surfaces and subdirect products
papers.abstract: This paper establishes strong profinite rigidity results for K\"ahler groups, showing that certain groups are determined within the class of residually finite K\"ahler groups by their profinite completion. Examples include products of surface groups and certain groups with exotic finiteness properties studied earlier by Dimca-Papadima-Suciu and Llosa Isenrich. Consequently, there are aspherical smooth projective varieties that are determined up to homeomorphism by their algebraic fundamental group. The main tool is the following: the holomorphic fibrations of a closed K\"ahler manifold over hyperbolic 2-orbifolds can be recovered from the profinite completion of its fundamental group. We also prove profinite invariance of the BNS invariant.

papers.title: Singular Levi-flats and holomorphic foliations on projective spaces
papers.abstract: We study codimension-one holomorphic foliations admitting invariant singular real-analytic Levi-flat varieties. Our main problem is to determine when the local meromorphic first integrals furnished by the Levi-flat geometry can be continued coherently and globalized. We introduce a pencil-singularity condition and a projective compatibility condition for local meromorphic parameters. In the projective plane these yield a characterization of foliations admitting a primitive rational first integral, while in higher-dimensional projective space they give a rational integrability criterion under a generic local-product hypothesis along the dicritical locus. We also obtain semi-global and Stein versions of these results. In a different direction, we study foliations admitting infinitely many invariant Levi-flat varieties and prove a Darboux-type alternative: either the foliation admits a rational first integral, or infinitely many Levi-flats contain a common invariant algebraic curve whose virtual holonomy is abelian. Under additional assumptions on the singularities, this leads to the existence of a closed rational, and in the absence of saddle-nodes a closed logarithmic, defining \(1\)-form.

papers.title: Chern classes of Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct closed Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds with non-vanishing Chern monomials. For every $n \geq 2$ and $\lceil n / 4 \rceil \leq m \leq \lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$, there exists a $(2 n + 1)$-dimensional example of signature $(\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor, \lceil n / 2 \rceil)$ on which all Chern monomials with positive indices at most $m$ and total weight at most $n - m$ are non-zero in cohomology with real coefficients. Taking $m = \lceil n / 4 \rceil$ gives examples with $c_{1}^{\lfloor 3 n / 4 \rfloor} \neq 0$. For $n = 4$ or $n \geq 6$, the latter examples show that the Chern-class vanishing theorem for strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds does not extend to the Levi non-degenerate case. In these dimensions, their underlying manifolds admit no strictly pseudoconvex CR structures. The construction uses circle bundles over products of integral pseudo-K\"{a}hler manifolds.

papers.title: Critical Point Theory for the Distance Function on PL-Spaces
papers.abstract: We study the (typical) singularities of the distance function from a point in the ambient space to a polytopal complex in Euclidean space. By means of the Goresky-MacPherson splitting we generalize the existing linear theory to the quadratic distance function. Critical points occur on `selected' strata of the PL-space, where normal Morse Data determine the change of topology. On the homology level there exist indices with multiplicities, combined in a Morse vector. We focus mainly on PL-manifolds. We give bounds, depending on the dimension of the strata. In low dimensions we describe singularity types. At the end we discuss relations with Discrete Morse Theory.

papers.title: Finding the Birman-Series set
papers.abstract: By a celebrated result of Birman and Series, the set of simple complete geodesics form a nowhere dense subset of a hyperbolic surface. We show that a segment of finite length is in a (small) neighborhood of this set if it can be "extended simply" in both directions for long enough. We deduce that, for large enough genus $g$, there exist surfaces with a Birman-Series set that is roughly $\frac{1}{g^{\sfrac{2}{3}}}$-dense.

papers.title: Quasipositive Braids, Presentations, and Garside Structures
papers.abstract: We provide a presentation of the braid group in which the generating set is the set of all positive half-twists, the relations are balanced positive relations, and every relation is conjugate to one in a finite list. We then prove that for any such presentation, its positive monoid is not isomorphic to the quasipositive braid monoid. Finally, we show that the quasipositive braid monoid has no proper Garside family. These results settle a problem of Calegari from the K3 problems list.

papers.title: Symmetries of colored Khovanov-Rozansky homology
papers.abstract: We construct an action of the positive half of the Witt algebra on colored $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-Khovanov-Rozansky homology and prove that this action is compatible with the functoriality of colored link homology. To establish this result, we use Bar-Natan's framework of canopolies to formulate and prove the relevant statements at the level of tangles.

papers.title: Recognizing oriented knots from finite quotients with one marked element
papers.abstract: For an oriented tame knot $K$, let $G_K$ be its group, with positive meridian $\mu_K$ and preferred longitude $\lambda_K$. We prove that the profinite completion $\widehat{G_K}$, marked by the conjugacy class of $\mu_K\lambda_K$, determines $K$ up to oriented equivalence. In fact, every isomorphism preserving this mark preserves the meridian and longitude with the same conjugator. The proof combines Xu's genuineness theorem with profinite JSJ theory and simultaneous boundary realization, and applies to satellite and composite knots. Consequently, Eisermann's colouring polynomials over all finite groups determine oriented knots.

papers.title: Thurston's Legacy at the Interface of Surface Dynamics, Train Tracks, and Arithmetic
papers.abstract: In this chapter, we discuss the interaction between low-dimensional dynamics, symbolic dynamics, and geometric topology, focusing on the algebraic characterization and asymptotic behaviour of stretch factors or equivalently pseudo-Anosov dilatations. We first review the algebraic foundations linking Perron--Frobenius theory, multi-variable Euclidean algorithms, and Lind's characterization of topological entropy for shifts of finite type, emphasizing recent constraints on the Perron--Frobenius degree of expansion constants. We then relate these dynamical invariants to the combinatorial world, examining train tracks for surfaces and automorphisms of free groups. Finally, we briefly review the relevance of fibered 3-manifolds, detailing how the Thurston norm, Fried's concavity theorem over fibered cones, and McMullen's Teichm\"uller polynomial come into play.

papers.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
papers.abstract: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.

papers.title: Self-intersecting sections of polar actions on simply connected manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct a polar action of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ on a closed simply connected $11$-manifold with a compact three-dimensional section that is not injectively immersed. The section is injective over the regular part and has two distinct local branches along a singular stratum. All isotropy groups are connected, and all orbits are simply connected. This gives a negative answer to the injectivity question raised by Grove and Ziller.

papers.title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
papers.abstract: The main result is an obstruction to the presence of contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension. As a first application, we prove a 5-dimensional analogue (under stronger assumptions) of a Reeb stability theorem for confoliations in dimension 3 due to Eliashberg and Thurston. Refining work of the first author with Cardona, we further give two new notions of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension generalizing the 3-dimensional notion of Eliashberg-Thurston. As a second application of our main theorem, we then give an example, in any ambient odd dimension, of a c-symplectic (and in fact strong symplectic) foliation that cannot be contact approximated, in either of these two senses. This relies on the property, of independent interest, that contact structures approximating (in these senses) a weakly c-symplectic confoliation are also weakly fillable. The proofs of all these statements rely on pseudo-holomorphic curve theory. Lastly, we describe several natural classes of examples of these types of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations.

papers.title: The Carath\'eodory metric on Teichm\"uller space of genus two surface
papers.abstract: Let $\Tei_{g,n}$ be the Teichm\"uller space of Riemann surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ marked points. It is conjectured that the Teichm\"uller and Carath\'{e}odory metrics coincide on a Teichm\"{u}ller disk exactly when every zero of the associated holomorphic quadratic differential (away from marked points) has even order. Gekhtman and Markovic verified this conjecture for $\Tei_{0,5}\cong \Tei_{1,2}$. We confirm the conjecture for $\Tei_{0,6}\cong\Tei_{2,0}$.

papers.title: On the Finiteness of Anosov flows on $3$-manifolds via Contact Geometry
papers.abstract: In dimension 3, following Eliashberg-Thurston and Mitsumatsu, one can associate a transverse pair of oppositely oriented contact structures to any Anosov flow. We show that when the ambient manifold is hyperbolic, the isotopy classes of these contact structures completely determine the flow up to isotopy orbit equivalence. This then implies that on any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, the number of Anosov flows modulo isotopy orbit equivalence is finite. This approach also yields an explicit bound on the number of orbit equivalence classes of Anosov flows in terms of the number of universally tight contact structures. In addition, we show finiteness of pseudo-Anosov flows for which the complement of the singular orbits is atoroidal and, in the non- hyperbolic case, we obtain a control on the dynamics of Anosov flows on the hyperbolic pieces of the JSJ-decomposition.

papers.title: Non-bi-orderable one-relator groups without generalized torsion
papers.abstract: We construct examples of non-bi-orderable one-relator groups without generalized torsion. This answers a question asked in [2].

papers.title: Finite type invariants in low degrees and the Johnson filtration
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of the Casson invariant $\lambda$, its square, and Othsuki's second invariant $\lambda_2$ as functions on the Johnson subgroup of the mapping class group. We show that since $\lambda$ and $d_2 = \lambda_2 - 18 \lambda^2$ are invariants that are morphisms on respectively the second and the third level of the Johnson filtration they never vanish on any level of this filtration. In contrast we prove that the invariant $\lambda_2-18\lambda^2 +3\lambda$ vanishes on the fifth level of the Johnson filtration, $\mathcal{M}_{g,1}(5)$, and as a consequence we prove that, for instance, the Poincar\'e homology sphere does not admit any Heegaard splitting with gluing map an element in $\mathcal{M}_{g,1}(5)$. Finally we determine a surgery formula for Othsuki's second invariant $\lambda_2$.

papers.title: Stable-norm boundary geometry on once-punctured tori
papers.abstract: We use normal-turn estimates to study the local and global geometry of the boundaries of stable-norm balls $B_X$ for complete finite-area hyperbolic once-punctured tori $X$. We show that the boundary $\partial B_X$ is a convex-geometric detector of exponential Diophantine approximation: rational directions give genuine corners with exponentially small exterior angles, while at an irrational direction $\beta$ the graph-flatness order admits an explicit formula in terms of the exponential rate at which rational directions approach $\beta$ and the $\ell^\infty$-radius of $B_X$ in the projective direction $\beta$. Thus irrational directions are not uniformly flat to infinite order, correcting the McShane--Rivin local picture. We also determine all possible irrational flatness orders and the size of the corresponding level sets. The computation of the rational corners unexpectedly yields a new McShane-type identity for the area of the dual body $B_X^*$: $$ \operatorname{Area}(B_X^*) = 4\sum_{\gamma} \ell_X(\gamma) \log\coth\left(\frac{\ell_X(\gamma)}{2}\right), $$ where the sum is over unoriented simple closed geodesics on $X$. As another global application, the normal-turn estimates also give a logarithmic-square bound for the number of integer points on the boundary of each dilated norm ball. Consequently, the number of simple closed geodesics of length exactly $L\geq2$ is at most $C_X(\log L)^2$. For the modular torus this yields $$ \#\lambda_M^{-1}(m)\leq C(\log\log(3m))^2 $$ for every Markoff number $m$, improving the previous logarithmic bounds for Markoff fibers.

papers.title: Multi-framed real monopole Floer theory
papers.abstract: This paper constructs a framed real monopole Floer homology for three-manifolds with involutions, marked with multiple basepoints. The relative gradings of these Floer homologies depend on the framing information and the paper gives a sufficient condition for the existence of relative mod two gradings. Assuming orientability and choices of orientations, this paper also proposes a definition of $\mathbf{Z}$-valued framed real Seiberg--Witten invariants for 4-manifolds with involutions, marked with circles.
